questions.q: What does the Nahuatl word 'mexcalli' (the root of 'mezcal') mean?
questions.story: The word mezcal comes from the Nahuatl 'mexcalli,' which means cooked agave.

questions.q: Which agave is the only one allowed for tequila?
questions.story: By law, tequila can be made from only one plant, Agave tequilana Weber blue variety, known as blue agave.

questions.q: How many Mexican states are in the tequila Appellation of Origin?
questions.story: Tequila can only be made in 181 municipalities across five states: Jalisco, Michoacán, Guanajuato, Nayarit and Tamaulipas.

questions.q: Which state is NOT in the tequila Appellation of Origin?
questions.story: Tequila can only be made in 181 municipalities across five states: Jalisco, Michoacán, Guanajuato, Nayarit and Tamaulipas.

questions.q: When was the tequila Appellation of Origin declaration published?
questions.story: Tequila's Appellation of Origin was declared on December 9, 1974, and celebrated its 50th anniversary in 2024.

questions.q: Since what year has mezcal had a Denomination of Origin?
questions.story: Mezcal has had its own Denomination of Origin since 1994. It covers all of Oaxaca, Guerrero, San Luis Potosí, Zacatecas and Durango, plus parts of Puebla, Michoacán, Tamaulipas and Guanajuato. A few newer additions, in Estado de México, Aguascalientes, Morelos and Sinaloa, are still under appeal.

questions.q: Which of these states is fully covered by the mezcal Denomination of Origin?
questions.story: Mezcal has had its own Denomination of Origin since 1994. It covers all of Oaxaca, Guerrero, San Luis Potosí, Zacatecas and Durango, plus parts of Puebla, Michoacán, Tamaulipas and Guanajuato. A few newer additions, in Estado de México, Aguascalientes, Morelos and Sinaloa, are still under appeal.

questions.q: What is the minimum aging for a reposado tequila?
questions.story: A reposado rests at least 2 months in oak. An añejo rests at least 1 year and an extra añejo at least 3 years, and both of those must use barrels of 600 liters or less.

questions.q: What is the minimum aging for an extra añejo tequila?
questions.story: A reposado rests at least 2 months in oak. An añejo rests at least 1 year and an extra añejo at least 3 years, and both of those must use barrels of 600 liters or less.

questions.q: What is the maximum barrel size for aging añejo tequila?
questions.story: A reposado rests at least 2 months in oak. An añejo rests at least 1 year and an extra añejo at least 3 years, and both of those must use barrels of 600 liters or less.

questions.q: A tequila labeled just 'Tequila' (not 100% agave) needs at least what share of blue agave sugars?
questions.story: '100% agave' tequila has to be bottled in Mexico, inside the origin region. Plain 'tequila' only needs 51% blue agave sugars.

questions.q: What is the harvest of the agave piña called?
questions.story: Harvesting the agave is called the jima: the piñas are cut once the plant is mature enough.

questions.q: About how long does it take to make tequila, from field to finished bottle?
questions.story: It can take 5 to 8 years to make tequila, counting from the field to the finished bottle.

questions.q: What is a mezcal distillery traditionally called?
questions.story: A mezcal distillery is called a palenque, and the person making it is a mezcalero.

questions.q: What is the large stone wheel used to crush cooked agave called?
questions.story: Traditionally the cooked agave is crushed by a big stone wheel called a tahona, pulled by an ox or donkey.

questions.q: Where does mezcal's signature smoky flavor come from?
questions.story: That smoky flavor in mezcal comes from roasting the piñas for days over hot rocks in earthen pits.

questions.q: Which state produces the most mezcal?
questions.story: Oaxaca makes more mezcal than any other state in Mexico.

questions.q: What fermented agave drink did the Aztecs make?
questions.story: The Aztecs considered agave sacred and fermented its juice into pulque long before anyone distilled it.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three official mezcal categories?
questions.story: Mexican law sorts mezcal into three categories: Mezcal, Mezcal Artesanal and Mezcal Ancestral, the most traditional of which is distilled over direct fire in clay pots.

questions.q: Which mezcal class is rested in glass for more than 12 months?
questions.story: Mezcal has a class tequila doesn't: 'Madurado en Vidrio,' rested in glass for more than 12 months, sometimes underground.

questions.q: What year was the Tequila agave landscape named a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
questions.story: The agave fields around Tequila are a UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed in 2006 and covering about 35,000 hectares between the Tequila Volcano and the Rio Grande valley.

questions.q: The 'tequila bat' is a common name for which species?
questions.story: The 'tequila bat,' the lesser long-nosed bat, pollinates agave flowers and can fly up to 100 km in one night.

questions.q: The tequila bat became the first bat ever removed from which list?
questions.story: Mexico took the tequila bat off its endangered species list in 2015, and it later became the first bat ever removed from the US endangered species list.

questions.q: What share of agave must be allowed to flower for Bat Friendly labeling?
questions.story: Bat Friendly tequila and mezcal comes from fields where producers let 5% of their agave flower for the bats, and more than 300,000 bottles have been released.

questions.q: Which Spanish king granted the first license to produce tequila, in 1795?
questions.story: In 1795 King Carlos IV of Spain granted José María Guadalupe Cuervo the first license to produce and distribute tequila.

questions.q: According to Casa Sauza, who bought La Antigua Cruz in 1873 and first called mezcal wine 'tequila'?
questions.story: In 1873 Don Cenobio Sauza bought La Antigua Cruz, one of the oldest distilleries in Tequila. Sauza says he was the first to call 'mezcal wine' by the name tequila.

questions.q: What date does Mexico now officially celebrate as National Tequila Day?
questions.story: Mexico now celebrates National Tequila Day every July 24, by a federal decree that replaced the old third-Saturday-of-March date.

questions.q: What is traditionally served alongside mezcal for sipping?
choices: Orange slices and sal de gusano
questions.story: Mezcal is traditionally sipped in small 'besitos,' or kisses, often with orange slices and sal de gusano, a worm salt.

questions.q: What does the CRT certify?
questions.story: The Consejo Regulador del Tequila, a non-profit founded on May 17, 1994, certifies every tequila and protects its Appellation of Origin.
